transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work, mostly on my sales reports. Like, I'll copy the wrong numbers down from the team dashboard, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. It's frustrating because it happens even when I really thought I went over everything.
Do you think you were paying attention when you made these mistakes or did your mind wander?

My mind definitely wanders. Like, when I'm trying to review call notes or look at the numbers, if there's just one conversation happening across the room, it pulls me right off track. Or even just a random thought about something going on at home... I get pulled away from what I'm doing before I even notice it happened.
Do you often find that you forget things that you were supposed to do?

Yeah, I do. It's not just at work, either. I forget regular life stuff too. Like, I'll completely forget to return a call from my attorney, or I won't remember to pay a bill until I get a late notice in the mail. And... well, I've forgotten to pick up things I promised my kids I'd bring home, which makes me feel pretty terrible. It just slips my mind entirely.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah, all the time. If I'm stuck sitting through a long meeting, it honestly feels like my body is just... buzzing on the inside. I can't just sit there. I have to keep shifting around in my chair, or I'll sit there tapping my foot. If it goes on too long, I usually just have to make up some excuse to get up and walk around for a minute.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

No, I don't really think so. I mean, I might get distracted easily, but I don't usually just jump into things without thinking. I'm pretty careful about making decisions, especially at work. So, no, acting on impulse isn't really a problem for me.
Have you been feeling overwhelmed or stressed lately?
Not really, no. I mean, work gets busy and life is life, but I wouldn't say I feel overwhelmed by it or overly stressed out. Just the normal amount, I guess. I handle it okay.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
No, not really. I mean, my mood has been fine. I don't really get down in the dumps or anything like that. So, no, feeling sad isn't really an issue for me.
Have you been experiencing any emotional difficulties, such as anxiety?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really feel anxious or nervous about things. I just kind of go about my day. So, no, anxiety hasn't been a problem.
When did you first start noticing these mistakes and difficulties with focus?

Well, it's really been a problem since I moved into the supervisor role at work. That was about... a year and two months ago, I'd say. That's when I first started noticing the mistakes and really having a hard time keeping my focus on things.
Have you experienced any significant life changes or stressors around the time you started noticing these difficulties with focus and making mistakes?

Not really, no. I mean, just the promotion to supervisor that I mentioned. That was a pretty big change, obviously, taking on all those new responsibilities and managing the sales guys. But other than that... no, nothing else comes to mind. Everything at home and in the rest of my life has stayed pretty much the same.
Have these difficulties with focus and making mistakes been consistent over the past year or have they varied in severity?

They've been pretty consistent, I think. I mean, it's not like some days are perfect and others are terrible. It's just a constant struggle to stay on top of things at work since I took the job. So, yeah, I'd say it's been a steady issue the whole time.
Have these difficulties with focus and mistakes at work affected your relationships with family or friends outside of work?

Yeah, it's definitely spilling over. At home, it just... it adds to the conflict, you know? My family, my friends, they feel like they can't count on me to follow through on things I say I'm going to do. And honestly, it's not just outside of work either. It's gotten to the point where my manager actually put it in my formal review. So it's pretty much affecting everything.
Have you had to change your daily routines or activities outside of work to cope with your difficulties with focus and mistakes?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven't consciously changed anything about my routine. I still try to do the same things I've always done—go to the gym, hang out with friends, take care of stuff around the house. It's just... harder to get it all done now. But I haven't started doing anything specific to cope with it, if that's what you mean. I'm mostly just trying to keep my head above water at work, honestly.
Have you experienced any significant emotional distress or impairment in social or occupational functioning as a result of your difficulties with focus and mistakes?

I'm not entirely sure what counts as significant emotional distress. I mean... I'm definitely stressed out, and it's really frustrating. And like I mentioned, it's already causing arguments at home and it showed up on my performance review at work, so it's definitely getting in the way of my life. But I wouldn't say I'm, you know, completely falling apart over it. I'm mostly just tired of the constant pressure of trying to keep up.
Have you ever experienced a period in your life where you didn't have these difficulties with focus and mistakes?

No, not really. I mean... I was like this as a kid, too. It's not a new thing. My mom actually still brings up the notes my teachers used to send home back in elementary school. They were always saying how I rushed through my work, or lost my homework... and that I talked out of turn a lot. Oh, and that I couldn't just stay in my seat without being reminded. So, yeah, it's pretty much always been like this for as long as I can remember.
Would you say that your difficulties with focus and mistakes have caused you problems that interfere with your work or relationships most of the time?

Yeah, I'd say so. Like I said, at work it's gotten to the point where my manager actually put it in my formal performance review, which isn't great. And at home... well, it definitely adds to the conflict. People feel like they just can't count on me to follow through on things I say I'll do. So, yeah, it definitely interferes most of the time.
Did you have any of these symptoms, like difficulty paying attention or feeling restless, when you were a teenager?

Yeah, like I was saying earlier, this isn't a new thing for me. I definitely had these issues as a teenager, and even before that. I was like this as a kid, too. My mom actually still brings up the notes my teachers used to send home back in elementary school. They were always saying how I rushed through my work, lost my homework, talked out of turn, and couldn't just stay in my seat without being reminded. So it's been going on pretty much my whole life.
Were you more active or fidgety than your peers when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. I think I already mentioned it, but I was definitely more active and fidgety than the other kids. Like I said, my mom still brings up those notes from my elementary school teachers. They were always complaining that I couldn't stay in my seat without being told, and that I was always talking out of turn, rushing through things, and losing my homework. So, yeah, I was definitely more restless than the other kids my age.
Have you had problems with restlessness or fidgeting in quiet activities like reading or watching a movie?

Yeah, I do. Even when I try to just relax quietly, it's tough. Like... if I'm watching a movie with my kids, or sitting through church, I can't just sit there. I end up whispering comments, checking my phone, or just getting up for no real reason at all.
